nodes.name: Li-doped oxide pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: NiFeCoLi/NF was prepared by brush-coating nickel felt (NF) with a mixed precursor solution containing Ni(NO₃)₂, Fe(NO₃)₃, Co(NO₃)₂, and LiNO₃ (mole ratio Ni:Fe:Co:Li = 9:1:1:1), followed by repeated pyrolysis cycles at 400°C in air. During each cycle, metal nitrates decompose to form oxides, which then chemically bond to the NF substrate, yielding a self-supported, multi-metal oxide coating layer (NiFeCoLi/NF).

nodes.source_text: As illustrated in Figure 1a, NiFeCoLi/NF was prepared by brush-coating nickel felt (NF) with a mixed precursor solution containing Ni(NO₃)₂, Fe(NO₃)₃, Co(NO₃)₂, and LiNO₃, followed by repeated pyrolysis cycles at 400°C in air. The mole ratio of Ni:Fe:Co:Li was 9:1:1:1.

nodes.name: Undoped oxide pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: NiFeCo/NF was synthesized identically to NiFeCoLi/NF but omitting LiNO₃ in the precursor solution (brush-coating nickel felt (NF) with a mixed precursor solution containing Ni(NO₃)₂, Fe(NO₃)₃, Co(NO₃)₂, followed by repeated pyrolysis cycles at 400°C in air).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show NiFeCoLi/NF retains the open 3D network of nickel felt with uniform ≈2 μm oxide layer and densely packed 200-500 nm polygonal nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images show that both NiFeCoLi/NF and NiFeCo/NF retain the open, 3D network of the nickel felt... High-resolution SEM image shows a densely packed, faceted 200 - 500 nm polygonal nanocrystals.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows well-defined lattice fringes in NiFeCoLi/NF with spacings of 0.212 nm and 0.246 nm corresponding to (200) and (111) planes of NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image shows well-defined lattice fringes in the NiFeCoLi/NF coating, with spacings of 0.212 and 0.246 nm corresponding to the (200) and (111) planes of NiO, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping confirm homogeneous distributions of Ni, Fe, Co, and O elements in NiFeCoLi/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and EDS mapping corroborate the homogeneous distributions of Ni, Fe, Co, and O.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns dominated by NiO peaks (PDF#04-0835); Rietveld refinement shows Li doping contracts unit-cell volume from 74.34 to 74.00 Å³ and shortens Ni-O bond from 2.102 to 2.099 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns for both samples are dominated by peaks indexed to NiO (PDF#04-0835)... Rietveld refinement of XRD patterns for NiFeCoLi/NF versus NiFeCo/NF reveals that Li doping contracts the unit-cell volume from 74.34 to 74.00 Å³.

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS mapping confirms uniform distribution of Li⁺ ions alongside other metal ions across NiFeCoLi/NF surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) mapping confirms a uniform distribution of Li⁺ ions alongside other metal ions across the NiFeCoLi/NF surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shifts to higher energy in NiFeCoLi/NF vs NiFeCo/NF and NiO, indicating elevated average Ni oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) shifts to higher energy in NiFeCoLi/NF compared to NiFeCo/NF and NiO, indicating an elevated average Ni oxidation state.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ni-O and Ni-Ni peaks moving to shorter radial distances upon Li doping in NiFeCoLi/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) shows Ni-O and Ni-Ni peaks moving to shorter radial distances upon Li doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Ni 2p spectrum shifts to higher binding energy after Li incorporation, confirming increased Ni valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) survey spectra confirm all constituent elements... the high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum shifts to higher binding energy after Li incorporation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show blue shift of Ni-O vibration (≈550 cm⁻¹) in NiFeCoLi/NF attributed to enhanced bond strength.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra display a blue shift of the Ni-O vibration (≈550 cm⁻¹) in NiFeCoLi/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS reveals substantially lower charge-transfer resistance (R_ct) for NiFeCoLi/NF compared to NiFeCo/NF and NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) reveals that the charge-transfer resistance (R_ct) of NiFeCoLi/NF is substantially lower than that of NiFeCo/NF and NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (C_dl) increases from 36.4 mF cm⁻² for NiFeCo/NF to 40.7 mF cm⁻² for NiFeCoLi/NF, indicating more accessible active sites upon Li doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the double-layer capacitance (C_dl), a proxy for electrochemically active surface area, increases from 36.4 to 40.7 mF cm⁻² (Figure S8, Supporting Information), indicating increased accessible active sites upon Li doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows valence-band maximum shifting from 1.18 to 0.96 eV below Fermi level and work function decreasing from 4.05 to 3.94 eV after Li doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Complementary ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) confirms the valence-band maximum shifting from 1.18 to 0.96 eV below the Fermi level... work function (ϕ) decreases from 4.05 to 3.94 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows NiOOH phase emerges at potentials >1.40 V vs RHE with Ni²⁺-O band disappearing and Ni³⁺-O signatures appearing ≈50 mV earlier than NiFeCo/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy was performed to track the structural evolution... NiFeCoLi/NF exhibits the NiOOH transition ≈50 mV earlier than NiFeCo/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS quantifies 0.245 ppm Ni leaching from NiFeCoLi/NF after 500 h vs 0.843 ppm from NiFeCo/NF after 300 h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) analysis quantifies only 0.245 ppm Ni leaching from NiFeCoLi/NF in 500 h electrolysis versus 0.843 ppm from NiFeCo/NF in 300 h electrolysis.
